headword: {直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}
reading: ちょくせつこうしょう

definitions.explanation: Negotiating with the other party in person, without going through an agent, intermediary, or higher authority. Common in labor disputes, business deals, diplomacy, and real-estate dealings.

examples.japanese: {直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}を{求|もと}めた。
{組合|くみあい}は{会社|かいしゃ}との{直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: The union entered into direct negotiations with the company.

examples.japanese: {仲介|ちゅうかい}{業者|ぎょうしゃ}を{通|とお}さず{直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}したほうが、{条件|じょうけん}を{細|こま}かく{決|き}められる。
examples.english: Negotiating directly rather than through a broker lets you settle the terms in more detail.

notes:
Used with する: {直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}する (to negotiate directly). The word often carries a slight sense of bypassing a normal channel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}する: to negotiate directly
- {直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}に{入|はい}る: to enter into direct talks
- {直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}を{求|もと}める: to demand direct negotiations
- {直接|ちょくせつ}{交渉|こうしょう}を{拒否|きょひ}する: to refuse direct negotiations

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {交渉|こうしょう}: negotiation — the general word, with no implication about the channel
- {仲介|ちゅうかい}: mediation, brokerage — going through a third party instead
- {団体|だんたい}{交渉|こうしょう}: collective bargaining — negotiation by a union as a body
